subject: science
passage: Woodlice, also called pill bugs, are small land-dwelling relatives of crabs and shrimp. They are usually found in damp places, such as under logs and stones. Biologist Kenji Morita hypothesizes that woodlice seek out these places because their bodies lose water quickly, so they dry out if they stay in open air for long.
stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Morita's hypothesis?

choices.A: Woodlice placed in a dry, dark box lived just as long as woodlice placed in a damp, dark box.
choices.B: Woodlice feed mainly on dead leaves and rotting wood found on the forest floor.
choices.C: Woodlice are most active at night, when birds and other predators have trouble finding them.
choices.D: Given a tray with damp and dry halves, equally dark, most woodlice gathered on the damp side.

explanation.why: Morita's hypothesis has two parts: woodlice dry out easily, and so they seek damp places. A test in which dampness is the only difference between two areas, and woodlice choose the damp one, supports it directly.
explanation.A: Incorrect. If woodlice survived just as well in dry air, they would not need damp places to avoid drying out, so this weakens the hypothesis.
explanation.B: Incorrect. What woodlice eat says nothing about whether they seek damp places to avoid drying out.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This gives a reason for their timing (avoiding predators), not evidence that they seek moisture.
explanation.D: Correct. Darkness was the same on both sides, so the woodlice chose the damp side because of the moisture.
